paragraphs: Flat Pizza with Chef Lucy, posted by Lily. Last Saturday, the Explorers went to the cooking class, and Chef Lucy showed us a simple dish. Her kitchen has a big window with a yellow curtain. Mia took the photos, and we made one pizza at each table. The recipe is easy, so please try it at home with an adult. You probably have most of the things in your kitchen. Read all the steps first, and then start to cook. It takes about half an hour. The kitchen will smell lovely.

Things you need for one pizza: One cup of flour. Half a cup of warm water. One spoon of oil. Three spoons of tomato sauce. A little cheese. A few thin slices of tomato. A bowl, a spoon, a pan, and an oven. Wash your hands before you start. Ask an adult to help you with the oven.

Step one: Put the flour, the water, and the oil in a bowl. Step two: Mix them with a spoon, and then with your hands. Now the dough is soft. Step three: Push the dough flat in a pan until it is as big as a plate. Chef Lucy said, "Do not make it too thin." "The pizza must be strong, because it has a lot of things on it."

Step four: Put the tomato sauce on the dough. Step five: Add the cheese and the slices of tomato. Step six: Ask an adult to put the pan in the oven for fifteen minutes. Our pans went into the oven at ten o'clock. Chef Lucy closed the curtain, because the sun was strong and the kitchen was hot. Then she gave each table a glass of cold water. We were hungry.

The pizza was ready, and the cheese was golden. It was hot, so we waited a few minutes. The taste was great, and Mia ate two pieces. Leo wants less cheese next time, because he does not like a strong taste. Teacher Kim liked it, too. I will make it at home on Sunday, and I will ask Mom to help me. Which things will you put on your pizza?
